notes: Smallest round-trip on Hermes: one plain-text prompt via the `hermes chat` REPL, one assistant reply, no tool use. Hermes writes no transcript file — the daemon observes the shared SQLite store at $HERMES_HOME/state.db (ProcessOwnedStore), where role='user' drives ready→working and an assistant row with finish_reason='stop' drives working→ready. The sessions row is INSERTed only on the first user message (~2s after launch), so there is no store-derived ready birth at launch: session_birth is anchored to recording start and left UNPINNED so the transient proc-<PID> pre-session that carries the ready birth cannot steal identity and cascade same_session_as failures, and turn1_done chains off turn1_start instead (the opencode ProcessOwnedStore shape). The 'no state_transition to waiting' invariant covers tool_calls_max:0 — a no-tool turn never gates on a permission ask. TotalTokens>0 is asserted via the observations block (tokens_nonzero), which reads the recording's metric vector; model and cost are deliberately unpinned because the recorded model depends on which config.yaml the run's HERMES_HOME carries — record fills observations.model and may add cost_nonzero once the recorded model is known to be priced.

text: A hermes session appears in ready shortly after launch; nothing ever enters waiting (no tool use)
A PID is bound to the session (Hermes is a Python console script, matched on the full command line)
The user prompt drives the store-backed session ready → working
The single turn completes back to ready on the same session (assistant row with finish_reason='stop' → turn_done)
